name: MS-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Thompson's long incumbency in a D+11 seat
Huge financial advantage: $1.4M on hand vs $36K
Minimal GOP challenger fundraising and no outside spending
model.rationale: Bennie Thompson holds a D+11 district with strong incumbency advantages and a massive cash edge over Ron Eller, who has raised only $45K. Prediction markets price Thompson near 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unexpectedly strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bennie Thompson, a longtime Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in Mississippi's 2nd District, a seat with an 11-point Democratic lean. He faces Republican Ron Eller and an independent, neither of whom has mounted a well-funded challenge. Thompson has raised about $771,000 and holds $1.4 million on hand, while Eller has raised under $46,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending in the race.

There are no public polls and no expert ratings, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets give Thompson roughly a 97% chance of winning. The district's partisan lean, Thompson's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial advantage all point to a comfortable Democratic win, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
